definitions.explanation: A series of successive victories without any losses in between. Used in sports, games, competitions, and other contests.

examples.japanese: ⟦チーム→チーム：03858_chiimu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{現在|げんざい}→現在：01556_genzai⟧5{連勝|れんしょう}⟦{中|ちゅう}→〜中：09840_chuu⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: The team is currently on a 5-game winning streak.

examples.japanese: {連勝|れんしょう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧10⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{止|と}まった→止まる：00555_tomaru⟧。
⟦{新記録|しんきろく}→新記録：16705_shinkiroku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧20{連勝|れんしょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{達成|たっせい}した→達成：04816_tassei⟧。
examples.english: They achieved a new record of 20 consecutive wins.

examples.japanese: {連勝|れんしょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{続|つづ}ける→続ける：01231_tsuzukeru⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦チーム→チーム：03858_chiimu⟧⟦{全体|ぜんたい}→全体：03314_zentai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{努力|どりょく}している→努力：03490_doryoku⟧。
examples.english: The whole team is working hard to keep the winning streak going.

examples.japanese: {連勝|れんしょう}⟦{街道|かいどう}→街道：14040_kaidou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{突|つ}き{進|すす}む→突き進む：07266_tsukisusumu⟧⟦エース→エース：28537_eesu⟧⟦ピッチャー→ピッチャー：09482_picchaa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{注目|ちゅうもく}→注目：03483_chuumoku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{集|あつ}まっている→集まる：01162_atsumaru⟧。
examples.english: Attention is focused on the ace pitcher who keeps marching along on a winning run.

notes:
{連勝|れんしょう} is a run of consecutive victories, chiefly in sports reporting but also in any repeated contest. A number attaches directly with no counter in between: 5{連勝|れんしょう} (five straight wins), 20{連勝|れんしょう} (twenty straight wins).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- As a ⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧-verb it takes no object — the winner is the subject: ⟦チーム→チーム：03858_chiimu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧5{連勝|れんしょう}⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧.
- N{連勝|れんしょう}⟦{中|ちゅう}→〜中：09840_chuu⟧: the streak is still running.
- {連勝|れんしょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{続|つづ}ける→続ける：01231_tsuzukeru⟧ / {連勝|れんしょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{伸|の}ばす→伸ばす：01973_nobasu⟧: keep it going, extend it.
- {連勝|れんしょう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{止|と}まる→止まる：00555_tomaru⟧: the streak ends. Note the intransitive verb — a winning streak is described as stopping by itself, not as being stopped, because no one ends their own run on purpose. A losing streak is the reverse: you ⟦{止|と}める→止める：00678_tomeru⟧ it.
- {連勝|れんしょう}⟦{記録|きろく}→記録：02490_kiroku⟧: a winning-streak record.

WORD FORMATION: {連|れん} (consecutive) + {勝|しょう} (victory). The same {連|れん} gives ⟦{連敗|れんぱい}→連敗：06529_renpai⟧ and ⟦{連続|れんぞく}→連続：03783_renzoku⟧.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{連敗|れんぱい}→連敗：06529_renpai⟧ is the antonym and takes the same number-plus-word shape.
- ⟦{連続|れんぞく}→連続：03783_renzoku⟧⟦{勝利|しょうり}→勝利：11795_shouri⟧ is the formal, non-sporting equivalent.
- In sumo a win and a loss are counted as ⟦{白星|しろぼし}→白星：19036_shiroboshi⟧ (white mark) and ⟦{黒星|くろぼし}→黒星：19294_kuroboshi⟧ (black mark), so streaks there are often reported with those words instead.

EXPRESSIONS: {連勝|れんしょう}⟦{街道|かいどう}→街道：14040_kaidou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{突|つ}き{進|すす}む→突き進む：07266_tsukisusumu⟧ — literally to charge down the winning-streak highway, a set sports-page phrase for a team or player on a long run.

CONTEXT: the word belongs to the vocabulary of ⟦プロ{野球|やきゅう}→プロ野球：08837_puroyakyuu⟧, ⟦{相撲|すもう}→相撲：00390_sumou⟧, ⟦サッカー→サッカー：04726_sakkaa⟧, and competitive games generally.
